I'm the one who originally pushed for disc golf support here  ( it landed January 2024 — OsmAnd-resources commit 2e54c440 / PR #1028 — keying on `sport=disc_golf`, which was the sensible choice at the time ). Two problems have since emerged with keying on the sport tag alone, and I'd like to propose extending the support to fix them:

**1. False positives — one course renders as a dozen POIs.** Only 57.8% of all `sport=disc_golf` objects are course features; the rest are fairways mapped as `leisure=pitch`, duplicates on tees/baskets/holes, and
floating tags (full carrier breakdown with method:
https://planetdg.com/osm/tagging/#sport-tag-carriers). Concrete example: around Plzeň (Czechia) there are 22 `sport=disc_golf` elements but only 2 actual courses — OsmAnd shows the DiscGolf Homolka course as ~a dozen basket icons named "1", "2", "3"…

**2. False negatives — and growing.** 18.5% of `leisure=disc_golf_course` features lack `sport=disc_golf` and are invisible in OsmAnd. This gap grows structurally: the iD editor stopped auto-adding `sport=disc_golf` to the course preset in July 2025 (openstreetmap/id-tagging-schema#1639, rationale: the leisure value implies the sport), so most newly mapped courses no longer get the tag.

**Request**: add `leisure=disc_golf_course` to `rendering_types.xml`, `poi_types.xml` and the default render style as the primary key for the disc golf POI/search entry (same icon), keeping `sport=disc_golf` for backward compatibility — ideally excluding `leisure=pitch` carriers from the POI icon to fix problem 1.

This mirrors how OsmAnd already treats golf (`leisure=golf_course` is the facility key). Happy to help test — I run https://planetdg.com, an OSM-based disc golf map; all statistics above with sources and method are
maintained at https://planetdg.com/osm/tagging/, and I can supply testregions.
title: Use `leisure=disc_golf_course` as primary key for Disc Golf POI and rendering

Golf tournament rows land on the golf tournament detail surface (not a generic market page), and the golf landing surfaces the upcoming intermediate PGA/tour events that are already in the DB.

## Two sub-bugs (Alex phone pass, SEQUENCE 000b item 3)

`TournamentCard` linked to `/sport/golf/{tour}/{slug}` (the generic `/sport/[sport]/[league]/[slug]` event/market template) instead of the golf-specific detail surface `/categories/golf/tournaments/[slug]` (powered by `/api/golf/tournaments/{slug}`, with leaderboard/outrights/props). Fixed: default href → `/categories/golf/tournaments/{slug}` (`components/TournamentCard.tsx:26`).

### (b) LIST GAP — upcoming intermediate events missing [DISPLAY bug, diagnosed; fix proposed]
NOT an ingestion gap. The DB has the markets: db-query (2026-06-15) shows **246 open golf futures markets**, including open tier-1 "Winner" markets for The Memorial Tournament, KLM Open, CJ Cup Byron Nelson, BMW Charity Pro-Am, and U.S. Women's Open — all resolving 2026-06-21 (upcoming, within a week of today).

But live `GET /api/golf` surfaces only **5 tournaments**: U.S. Open, The Open Championship, Presidents Cup, LIV Golf, "Rory McIlroy Majors in 2026" — all majors/named/prop events. The weekly intermediate events do NOT surface.

**Surfaced vs expected: 5 surfaced vs (5 + at least ~5 upcoming weekly events present in the DB).**

**Drop point (grounded):** `routes/golf.py` aggregation `get_golf`. The 5 that surface are multi-outcome winner markets (DataGolf/Polymarket) summing ~1.0. The missing weekly events are covered mainly by **Kalshi independent-binary winner markets** (per-golfer Yes/No, or a multi-outcome market whose probabilities sum well over 100% — gotcha #23). ## Problem
`KALSHI_FUTURES_TICKER_TO_SPORT_KEY` (sport_keys.py) maps only SPECIFIC golf prop prefixes via `startswith`. Live data shows **47 distinct `kxpga*` prefixes, all golf**, but many are NOT in the map (e.g. `kxpga3ball`, `kxpga5ball`, `kxpgaroundscore`, `kxpgatop40`, `kxpgaplayercat`, `kxpgastrokemargin`, `kxpgaholescore`, `kxpgauso`, `kxpgaplayoff`, `kxpgar1top20`/`r2top5`/`r3top5`, ...). Kalshi ingest has no LLM, and men's "U.S. Open" is not a golf name-rule, so newly-ingested off-map series sit `'other'` (invisible to /api/golf) until the 8 AM UTC `recategorize_other_task` LLM pass. (Current classification gap = 0 only because that LLM pass has already run.)

## Fix (this issue)
Add a generic `"kxpga": "golf"` catch-all to the golf section of the futures ticker map — `kxpga` is unambiguously PGA golf (tennis is `kxatp*`; verified 0 non-golf kxpga in prod), so it deterministically classifies all current + future men's-PGA prop series at ingest. Do NOT add a bare "us open"/"u.s. open" name-rule (collides with TENNIS US Open). No migration. Unit test: each off-map prefix → golf; tennis "US Open" NOT golf.

The OSM/OpenGolfAPI crawler is US-only by construction: `scripts/crawl/util.ts` `STATE_BBOX` contains only the 48 contiguous-US state bounding boxes, and the OSM modes error on any region without a configured bbox. The full US is already crawled (all 48 states, all phases, 2026-05-02). To expand coverage internationally:

- **Discovery (`osm` mode) works for ANY bbox** — Overpass returns `leisure=golf_course` in any lat/lng box. So add international regions to a bbox table and run `osm` against them. Chunk the world into manageable sub-regions (per-country, or smaller for big countries) — Overpass times out on huge bboxes (the per-US-state split exists for this reason).
- **Watch the key collision:** `STATE_BBOX` keys are 2-char and `CA` already = California. ISO-2 country codes collide (CA = Canada). Use a separate `REGION_BBOX` map or prefixed keys.
- **Enrich/OpenGolfAPI is US-state-keyed** (`/courses/state/:STATE`) — won't work internationally. Skip it for non-US; get ratings from **GolfCourseAPI** instead (100+ countries) via `scripts/backfill-ratings.ts`, which is already region-agnostic.
- Suggested first regions: Canada, GB&I (England/Scotland/Wales/Ireland), Australia, NZ, Western Europe.

Out of scope for v1 launch; tracked for later.

- Test with 5+ real products and verify price accuracy

so I got it down to 1022 bytes and I think I can do more with a bigger rethink. this was mostly just "try to shave 1 byte, test, repeat," with some reading of SeaBIOS/qemu code to be sure. I annotated the new tricks I used. It took me 133 iterations to get here, hence the need for the exact text test I had submitted.

This will not work on non-SeaBIOS/qemu so I am not happy with it, but you said you were interested.  I do think 1024 is achievable without making it rely on those hacks. If I can hit my own personal size target I'll go back and undo the seabios hacks.

bits 16
org 0x7c00


;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;; Model parameters                                                           ;;
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
%define DIM 64
%define DIM_LOG 6
%define HIDDEN 172
%define LAYERS 5
%define HEADS 8
%define KV_HEADS 4
%define VOCAB 512               ; Vocab size
%define SEQ 512                 ; Maximum input sequence length
%define HEAD_DIM (DIM / HEADS)
%define KV_DIM (KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM)
%define TOKEN_COUNT 300         ; Maximum token count to generate


;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;; Model layout                                                               ;;
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
%define MODEL_BASE 0x2000

; Sizes in paragraphs

; Precomputed lookup tables (exp and silu)
%define P_LUT       0x180       ; 6144 bytes
%define P_TOKEN_EMB (VOCAB * DIM * 4 / 16)
; Attention pre-RMSNorm weights
%define P_RMS_ATT   (LAYERS * DIM * 4 / 16)

; Attention QKV projection (concatenated WQ, WK, WV matrices)
; Stored as int8 weights with an inline per-layer scale dword
%define P_WQKV_Q_L  0x210
%define P_WQKV_Q    (LAYERS * P_WQKV_Q_L)
%define P_WQKV_S    0

; Attention output projection
%define P_WO_Q_L    0x110
%define P_WO_Q      (LAYERS * P_WO_Q_L)
%define P_WO_S      0

; Feed-forward, Pre-RMSNorm weights
%define P_RMS_FFN   (LAYERS * DIM * 4 / 16)
; FFN down-projection
%define P_W2_Q_L    0x2C0
%define P_W2_Q      (LAYERS * P_W2_Q_L)
%define P_W2_S      0

; FFN Gate and up-projection (W1 and W3 concatenated)
%define P_W13_Q_L   0x570
%define P_W13_Q     (LAYERS * P_W13_Q_L)
%define P_W13_S     0
; New trick: duplicate each tensor's shared Q8 scale at offset 0 of every layer
; slot so matmul can select layer and scale together.

; Final output RMSNorm weight
%define P_RMS_FINAL (DIM * 4 / 16)

; RoPE frequencies
; interleaved cos/sin pairs for sequence length up to 512
%define P_FREQ      (SEQ * (HEAD_DIM/2) * 2 * 4 / 16)

; Dynamic Segments
%define W_TOKEN_EMB (MODEL_BASE + P_LUT)
%define W_RMS_ATT   (W_TOKEN_EMB + P_TOKEN_EMB)
%define W_WQKV_Q    (W_RMS_ATT + P_RMS_ATT)
%define W_WQKV_S    (W_WQKV_Q + P_WQKV_Q)
%define W_WO_Q      (W_WQKV_S + P_WQKV_S)
%define W_WO_S      (W_WO_Q + P_WO_Q)
%define W_RMS_FFN   (W_WO_S + P_WO_S)
%define W_W2_Q      (W_RMS_FFN + P_RMS_FFN)
%define W_W2_S      (W_W2_Q + P_W2_Q)
%define W_W13_Q     (W_W2_S + P_W2_S)
%define W_W13_S     (W_W13_Q + P_W13_Q)
%define W_RMS_FINAL (W_W13_S + P_W13_S)
%define W_FREQ_CIS  (W_RMS_FINAL + P_RMS_FINAL)
%define VOCAB_PTR   (W_FREQ_CIS + P_FREQ)


;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;; Scratch data (ES)                                                          ;;
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
%define R_X       0x0000    ; FP16.16[DIM]
%define R_XB      0x0100    ; FP16.16[DIM]
%define R_HB      0x0200    ; FP16.16[2*HIDDEN], overlaps dead R_QKV
%define R_QKV     0x0200    ; 384 bytes (Q=64, K=16, V=16), overlaps dead R_HB
%define R_XB2     0x0300    ; FP16.16[DIM], overlaps dead K/V tail of R_QKV

; Global State Variables
%define R_MAX     0x0100    ; dword, overlaps dead R_XB during logits
%define R_BEST    0x0104    ; word
%define CUR_LAYER 0x07E6    ; word
%define CUR_POS   0x07E8    ; word

%define R_ATT     0x0800    ; FP16.16[TOKEN_COUNT*HEADS]
; New trick: alias scratch by lifetime, not by subsystem.
    

; Cache Segments
%define KC_SEG 0x0840
%define KS_SEG 0x1C40
%define VC_SEG 0x8600
%define VS_SEG 0x9A00

; Best for hot code
%macro Q16_SHIFT_INLINE 0
    shrd eax, edx, 16
%endmacro
    

;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;; Boot sector                                                                ;;
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
; The boot sector loads the second stage and model data from disk.
; It also contains the main inference loop and utility subroutines.
entry:
    ; New trick: steal SeaBIOS entry AX=0xAA55 to seed SP in 1 byte.
    xchg sp, ax

    ; Load stage2
    mov bh, 0x7E
    mov ax, 0x0202              ; AH=02 read, AL=2 sectors
    mov cl, 2                   ; assume CH=0, sector 2
    int 0x13
    mov ax, 0x2000              ; LUT segment
    mov fs, ax
    ; New trick: build the DAP on the stack, then reload its final seg:off with LES
    ; to recover runtime ES and BX for free.
    push 3
    push ax
    push es
    push 64
    push 0x10
    mov si, sp

    ; Load the model at 0x2000:0
    mov cl, 12

.load_model:
    mov ah, 0x42
    int 0x13

    add dword [si + 6], 0x00400800 ; add 64 to lba, 0x800 to segment
    loop .load_model

    ; Recover ES=0x8000 and BX=0 from the final DAP segment:offset pair.
    les bx, [si + 4]

start_inference:
    inc bx                      ; BOS

.gen_loop:
    call forward
    jbe $
    call print_token
    inc word [es:CUR_POS]
    jmp .gen_loop


; Inverse square root approximation
; in  EBP: x (FP16.16)
; out EBP: 1/sqrt(x) (FP16.16)
; Clobbers: ecx
inv_sqrt:
    ; Initial guess from bit position: y ~= 2^((48-bsr(x))/2)
    bsr ecx, ebp
    neg cl
    add cl, 48
    shr cl, 1
    xor eax, eax
    bts eax, ecx                ; eax = (1<<ecx), initial y
    mov cl, 5                   ; Should be good enough

; Newton-Raphson: y = y * (3 - x*y^2) / 2
.loop:
    mov esi, eax                ; esi = y
    mul eax                     ; edx:eax = y^2
    call q16_shift              ; convert to FP16.16
    mul ebp                     ; edx:eax = x*y^2
    call q16_shift              ; convert to FP16.16
    neg eax                     ; eax = -x*y^2
    add eax, 3*65536            ; eax = 3 - x*y^2 (FP16.16)
    mul esi
    call q16_shift              ; eax = y*(3 - x*y^2) (FP16.16)
    shr eax, 1                  ; / 2
    loop .loop
.done:
    xchg eax, ebp
    ret

; rmsnorm helper: sets up DS and BX before doing rmsnorm logic
; in AX:      weight segment base
; in ES:DI:   output buffer
zero_di_do_rmsnorm:
        xor di, di
do_rmsnorm:
        ; New trick: store CUR_LAYER as layer*16 so helpers can add it directly.
        add ax, [es:CUR_LAYER]
        mov ds, ax
        xor bx, bx

; Compute RMSNorm: out[i] = x[i] * w[i] / sqrt(mean(x^2) + epsilon)
; in  ES:DI: output buffer (FP16.16[DIM])
; in  ES:0:  input x (R_X, FP16.16[DIM])
; in  DS:0:  weights w (FP16.16[DIM])
rmsnorm:
    xor ebp, ebp                ; ebp = sum of squares accumulator
    mov cl, DIM
    xor si, si                  ; SI=0, points to ES:R_X
    push si                     

; 1. Compute sum of squares
.sum:
    es lodsd                    ; eax = x[i], SI+=4
    imul eax                    ; edx:eax = x[i]^2
    call q16_shift              ; eax = x[i]^2 in FP16.16
    add ebp, eax                ; ebp += x[i]^2
    loop .sum

.eps:
    ; ss = (sum / DIM) + epsilon
    shr ebp, DIM_LOG            ; ebp = sum/DIM
    inc bp ; epsilon

    call inv_sqrt               ; ebp = 1/sqrt(ss) in FP16.16

    pop si                      ; restore SI to R_X
    mov cl, DIM

; 2. Normalize and apply weights
.norm:
    es lodsd              ; eax = x[i], SI += 4
    imul ebp              ; eax = x[i] * (1/sqrt(ss))
    call q16_shift
    imul dword [bx]       ; eax *= w[i]
    call q16_shift        ; eax = x[i] * w[i] / sqrt(ss)
    add bx, 4             ; advance weight pointer
    stosd                 ; write to output, DI += 4
    loop .norm
.done:
    xchg di, bx
    ret

; matmul helper:
; in AX:   base_Q
; in CL:   layer stride
; in CH:   cols
; in DX:   rows
; ES:DI: input vector
; ES:BX: output vector
do_matmul:
    ; New trick: packed matmul ABI. CL=stride/16, CH=cols, DX=rows, and the chosen
    ; layer slot begins with its duplicated scale dword.
    push cx                    ; save cols while deriving layer segments
    xor ch, ch
    imul cx, [es:CUR_LAYER]    ; cx = layer * stride (paragraphs)
    add ax, cx                 ; ax = weight base + layer*stride
    mov ds, ax                 ; DS = this layer's int8 weight segment
    xor si, si
    mov ebp, [si]              ; layer tensor scale
    mov si, 4                  ; first weight byte
    pop cx
    xchg ax, dx                 ; ax = rows
    shr cx, 8                  ; cx = cols

; Multiply an int8 matrix by a FP16.16 vector
; in DS:SI:     int8 weight matrix (row-major)
; in ES:DI:     input vector (FP16.16[COLS])
; in ES:BX:     output vector (FP16.16[ROWS])
; in AX:         rows
; in CX:         cols
; in EBP:       FP16.16 scale factor for dequantization
matmul:

; For each output element
.row:
    push ax                     ; save row count
    push cx                     ; save cols
    push di                     ; save input vector base
    push bx                     ; save out

    xor ebx, ebx                ; ebx = dot product accumulator

; dot product: sum(weight[col] * input[col])
.dot:
    lodsb                       ; al = int8 weight, SI += 1
    ; sign-extend
    cbw
    cwde
    imul dword [es:di]          ; edx:eax = weight * input[col]
    scasd                       ; di += 4
    add ebx, eax                ; accumulate low 32 bits (should be safe for DIM=64)
    loop .dot

; dequantize: (acc * scale) >> 16
    xchg eax, ebx
    imul ebp                    ; edx:eax = acc * scale
    call q16_shift              ; eax = result in FP16.16

; Store result
    pop di                      ; output pointer
    stosd                       ; store result and advance output pointer
    mov bx, di                  ; keep advanced output pointer for caller/next row
    pop di
    pop cx
    pop ax
    dec ax
    jnz .row

    ret

; Add the matmul output into R_X in-place
; in ES:BX: matmul output
; Convenience wrapper around vadd for post-matmul accumulation (saves bytes)
vadd_rx:
    dec bh                      ; matmul leaves BX one DIM vector past output
    xchg si, bx                 ; grab pointer from matmul
    xor di, di                  ; R_X

; Vector addition: ES:DI += ES:SI for DIM FP16.16 elements
; in ES:SI: src vector (FP16.16[DIM])
; in ES:DI: dest vector (FP16.16[DIM])
vadd:
    mov cl, DIM
.lp:
    es lodsd                    ; eax = *SI, SI += 4
    add [es:di], eax            ; *DI += eax
    scasd                       ; DI += 4
    loop .lp
    ret

; Apply RoPE to a vector in-place.
; Rotates each consecutive pair (x0, x1) by the angle for its position,
; using precomputed interleaved (cos, sin) pairs in the frequency table.
; in ES:DI: vector to rotate (FP16.16), modified in place
; in CX:     number of heads to process
apply_rope:
    ; New trick: lay Q and K back-to-back so one RoPE walk handles both.
    imul si, [es:CUR_POS], 32   ; si = CUR_POS * 32 (8 bytes per pair * 4 pairs per head)
    push W_FREQ_CIS
    pop ds                      ; DS = freq table


.head_loop:
    push si                     ; save freq table offset
    push cx                     ; save head counter
    mov cl, 4                   ; 4 pairs per head

.pair_loop:
    ; Load sin and cos values
    lodsd                       ; eax = cos, SI += 4
    xchg eax, ebp               ; ebp = cos
    lodsd                       ; eax = sin, SI += 4
    xchg eax, ebx               ; ebx = sin

    ; Rotate (x0, x1):
    ;   new_x0 = x0*cos - x1*sin
    ;   new_x1 = x0*sin + x1*cos
    mov eax, [es:di+4]          ; x1
    imul ebx                    ; x1*sin
    call q16_shift
    push eax                    ; stack = x1*sin

    mov eax, [es:di]            ; x0
    imul ebp                    ; x0 * cos
    call q16_shift
    pop edx                     ; edx = x1*sin
    sub eax, edx                ; new_x0 = (x0*cos)-(x1*sin)
    xchg [es:di], eax           ; store new_x0, recover old x0
    imul ebx                    ; x0*sin
    call q16_shift
    push eax                    ; stack = x0*sin

    mov eax, [es:di+4]          ; x1
    imul ebp                    ; x1*cos
    call q16_shift
    pop edx                     ; edx = x0*sin
    add eax, edx                ; eax = x0*sin+x1*cos

    mov [es:di+4], eax          ; store new_x1

    add di, 8                   ; advance to next (x0, x1) pair
    loop .pair_loop

    pop cx
    pop si
    loop .head_loop
    ret



; Print the token string from the corresponding number.
; in BX: Token number
print_token:
    ; New trick: tokenizer is a u16 offset table into NUL-terminated strings.
    push VOCAB_PTR              ; DS = VOCAB_PTR
    pop ds
    push bx
    shl bx, 1
    mov si, [bx]
    mov ah, 0x0E                ; teletype out
.print_str:
    lodsb                       ; c=VOCAB_PTR[SI++]
    test al, al
    jz .done                    ; stop at NULL
    int 0x10                    ; print c
    jmp .print_str
.done:
    pop bx
    ret

; Set DS to a segmented address for KV cache access.
; two entry points for different cache stride sizes.
; in DX:  base segment
; out DS: base + (CUR_LAYER * stride)
set_seg_1024:
    mov cl, 6
    db 0x3D                     ; Nice!
set_seg_128:
    mov cl, 3
.do_seg:
    push ax
    mov ax, [es:CUR_LAYER]
    shl ax, cl                  ; ax = CUR_LAYER * stride
    add dx, ax                  ; dx = base + layer offset
    mov ds, dx                  ; DS = target segment
    pop ax
    ret

quant_kv_cache:
    ; New trick: K and V share one quantization body with tiny wrappers.
    mov ax, KC_SEG
    call .quant
    mov ax, VC_SEG
 .quant:
    push ax
    add ah, 0x14
    push ax
    mov cl, KV_DIM
    push si
    xor ebx, ebx
    jmp quant_cache

; Compute the byte offset into the KV cache for a given token and KV head
; The cache layout is [token][kv_head][DIM] with each element being int8
; in DI:   t (token position)
; in BP:   h (attention head index)
; out BX:  t * KV_DIM + kvh * HEAD_DIM
call_set_seg_1024_jmp_get_kv_offset:
    call set_seg_1024
get_kv_offset:
    imul bx, di, 32 ; bx = t * 32 (KV_DIM bytes per token)
    imul cx, bp, 4
    and cl, 0x18 ; cx = (h / 2) * HEAD_DIM
    add bx, cx ; bx = offset of this token's KV head slice
    ret

; Compute a pointer into the attention score buffer.
; R_ATT layout is [head][token], each element being FP16.16
; in BP:  h (head index)
; in DI:  t (token position)
; out SI: &R_ATT[h][t], DX: t * 4
get_att_ptr:
    inc bp
    imul si, bp, 2048      ; (h + 1) * 2048, with R_ATT at 0x0800
    dec bp
    imul dx, di, 4         ; dx = t * 4 (4 bytes per score)
    add si, dx             ; SI = &R_ATT[h][t]
    ret

; New trick: boot-tail parasites. Tiny hot-path tails live in spare boot bytes
; and stage2 jumps into them instead of carrying duplicate epilogues locally.
; It is slower to always call this function but it saves two bytes each time!
q16_shift:
    shrd eax, edx, 16
    ret

set_ds_token_emb_tail:
    mov ds, ax
zero_si_zero_di_jmp_get_pos_count:
    xor si, si

zero_di_jmp_get_pos_count:
    xor di, di
get_pos_count:
    mov cx, [es:CUR_POS]
    inc cx
    ret

quant_cache_div_tail:
    cdq                         ; sign-extend into edx
    idiv ebp                    ; eax = round(x/scale), clamped to int8

quant_cache_store_tail:
    mov [bx], al                ; store quantized byte

inc_bx_q_lp_tail:
    inc bx

quant_cache_q_lp_tail:
    loop quant_cache.q_lp
    ret

silu_gate_q16_tail:
    call q16_shift              ; shift back to FP16.16
    stosd                       ; gate[i] = res, DI += 4

silu_gate_loop_tail:
    loop silu_gate.lp

silu_gate_tail:
    xchg di, bx
    pop di
    ret

set_ds_token_emb:
    imul ax, bx, 16
    add ax, W_TOKEN_EMB
    jmp set_ds_token_emb_tail

_bootsector_end:
%assign bootsector_size _bootsector_end - $$
%warning boot sector is bootsector_size bytes.
times 510 - ($ - $$) db 0
dw 0xAA55



;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
;; Sector 1 and 2                                                             ;;
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;

; SiLU gating: out[i] = silu(gate[i]) * up[i]
; where silu(x) = x * sigmoid(x), looked up from a precomputed table
silu_gate:
    mov di, R_HB                ; DI = gate vector
    push di
    mov si, R_HB+HIDDEN*4       ; SI = up vector
    mov cl, HIDDEN
.lp:
    ; Compute silu_lut index from gate[i]
    mov eax, [es:di]            ; eax = gate[i] (FP16.16)
    sar eax, 8                  ; byte offset into silu_lut
    and al, 0xFC
    add ah, 0x10
    xchg ax, bx                 ; bx = silu_lut byte offset

    ; Multiply by up[i] and store in gate[i]
    es lodsd                    ; eax = up[i]
    imul dword [fs:bx]          ; eax = up[i] * silu(gate[i])
    jmp silu_gate_q16_tail

quant_cache:
    ; Find max absolute value
.max_lp:
    es lodsd
    cdq                         ; sign-extend into edx
    xor eax, edx
    sub eax, edx                ; eax = abs(eax)
    cmp ebx, eax
    cmovl ebx, eax              ; new max
    loop .max_lp
    pop si

; Compute scale (max / 127)
.do_scale:
    xchg eax, ebx
    cdq
    mov cl, 127
    idiv ecx                    ; eax = max / 127
    xchg ebp, eax               ; ebp = scale

    ; store scale
    pop dx
    call set_seg_128            ; DS = scale cache segment for this layer
    imul bx, [es:CUR_POS], 4
    mov [bx], bp                ; scale_cache[bx] = scale

    ; quantize and cache
    pop dx
    call set_seg_1024           ; DS = int8 cache segment for this layer
    shl bx, 3                   ; bx = CUR_POS * 32
    mov cl, KV_DIM
.q_lp:
    es lodsd
    jmp quant_cache_div_tail

; Full forward pass of the transformer for one token.
; in BX:  input token index
; out BX: predicted token
forward:
    ; Load token embedding into R_X
    call set_ds_token_emb
    mov cl, DIM * 2             ; dword
    rep movsw                   ; R_X = embedding[token]

    mov [es:CUR_LAYER], cx      ; cx is 0

.layer:
    ; Normalize input before attention
    mov ax, W_RMS_ATT
    call do_rmsnorm             ; R_XB = rmsnorm(R_X, w_rms_att[layer])



    ; Project normalized input to Q, K, V simultaneously
    mov ax, W_WQKV_Q
    mov cx, (DIM << 8) | (P_WQKV_Q_L >> 4)
    mov dx, DIM + 2*KV_DIM      ; rows = Q+K+V
    call do_matmul              ; R_QKV = [Q | K | V] = w_wqkv * R_XB


    ; Apply RoPE to Q and K
    mov di, R_QKV
    mov cl, HEADS + KV_HEADS
    call apply_rope             ; rotate Q and K

    ; Quantize and cache K and V for this position
    mov si, R_QKV + DIM*4
    call quant_kv_cache         ; KC/VC[layer][pos] = quantize(K/V)


    ; Compute attention scores, softmax and weight sum of V
    call attention              ; R_XB = attention(Q, KC, VC)

    ; Project attention output back to DIM
    mov ax, W_WO_Q
    mov cx, (DIM << 8) | (P_WO_Q_L >> 4)
    mov dx, DIM
    mov di, R_XB
    mov bh, R_XB2 >> 8
    call do_matmul              ; R_XB2 = w_wo * R_XB

    ; Residual connection
    call vadd_rx                ; R_X += R_XB2

    ; FFN

    ; Normalize before FFN
    mov ax, W_RMS_FFN
    call do_rmsnorm             ; R_XB = rmsnorm(R_X, w_rms_ffn[layer])

    ; Project up to hidden dim
    mov ax, W_W13_Q
    mov cx, (DIM << 8) | (P_W13_Q_L >> 4)
    mov dx, 2*HIDDEN
    call do_matmul              ; R_HB = [gate | up] = w_w13 * R_XB

    ; Apply SiLU gating
    call silu_gate

    ; Project back down to DIM
    mov ax, W_W2_Q
    mov cx, (HIDDEN << 8) | (P_W2_Q_L >> 4)
    mov dx, DIM
    call do_matmul              ; R_XB = w_w2 * R_HB

    ; Residual connection
    call vadd_rx                ; R_X + R_XB

    ; Go to next layer
    add byte [es:CUR_LAYER], 16
    cmp byte [es:CUR_LAYER], LAYERS * 16
    jl .layer

    ; Final normalization
    mov ax, W_RMS_FINAL - LAYERS * 16
    call zero_di_do_rmsnorm     ; R_X = rmsnorm(R_X, w_rms_final)

    ; Compute logits and pick best token (use greedy argmax)
    xor bx, bx                       ; BX = token index

; logit computation: dot(R_X, embedding[i])
; Since the model uses weight tying, the output projection reuses
; the token embedding table the logit for token i is just the
; dot product of the final hidden state with embedding[i].
.lm_loop:
    call set_ds_token_emb

    xor ebp, ebp                ; ebp dot accumulator
    mov cl, DIM
.dot:
    lodsd                       ; eax = embedding[i][j], SI += 4
    imul dword [es:di]          ; edx:eax = embedding[i][j] * R_X[j]
    call q16_shift              ; inline this for more perf, but it'll cost you two bytes!
    add ebp, eax                ; accumulate
    scasd                       ; DI += 4
    loop .dot

; argmax, just track the highest scoring token
    cmp ebp, [es:di + R_MAX - DIM*4]
    jle .skip_max
.set_max:
    xchg eax, ebp
    stosd
    xchg ax, bx
    stosw
    xchg ax, bx
.skip_max:
    inc bx
    test bh, VOCAB >> 8
    jz .lm_loop                 ; next token

    mov bx, [es:di + R_BEST - R_MAX]
    cmp bx, 2                   ; check for BOS or EOS
    ret

; Compute multi-head grouped-query attention for the current position.
; Reads Q from R_QKV, K/V from the quantized KV cache.
; Output is written into R_XB (one HEAD_DIM slice per head).
attention:
    ; New trick: attention helpers return reusable indices/pointers instead of
    ; making callers recompute them.
    mov bp, HEADS-1             ; bp = h (head index, HEADS-1..0)
.head_loop:

    ; 1.QK dot products
    ; For each past token t, compute a_t = dot(Q_h, K_t) * scale
    ; and store in R_ATT[h][t]
    call zero_di_jmp_get_pos_count ; process tokens t = 0..CUR_POS inclusive, DI = t
.t_loop:
    push cx                     ; save token counter

    ; load K vector for token T, KV head kvh = h/2
    mov dx, KC_SEG
    call call_set_seg_1024_jmp_get_kv_offset ; DS = K cache, BX = offset of K[t][kvh]

    ; Load Q vector for head h
    imul ax, bp, 32             ; h * 32
    mov ah, R_QKV >> 8
    xchg ax, si                 ; SI = &Q[h]

    push bp                     ; save h
    mov cl, HEAD_DIM
    xor ebp, ebp                ; acc

; dot(Q_h, K_t), K is int8, Q is FP16.16
.dot_loop:
    movsx edx, byte [bx]        ; edx = K
    inc bx
    es lodsd                    ; eax = Q[h][i], SI += 4
    imul edx                    ; edx:eax = Q[h][i] * K[t][i]
    add ebp, eax                ; accumulate (low 32 bits enough for HEAD_DIM=8)
    loop .dot_loop

.dot_done:
    xchg eax, ebp
    pop bp                      ; restore h

    ; Dequantize: multiply by K scale for token t
    call get_att_ptr            ; SI = &R_ATT[h][t], DX = t * 4
    push si
    movzx esi, dx
    mov dx, KS_SEG
    call set_seg_128            ; DS = K scale cache for this layer
    imul dword [si]             ; scale_kt lives in the low word of a padded dword slot
    call q16_shift              ; eax = dot * scale_kt

    ; multiply by 1/sqrt(HEAD_DIM) ~= 23170
    mov si, 23170
    imul esi
    call q16_shift              ; eax = a_t (attention score, FP16.16)

    ; store score in R_ATT[h][t]
    pop si
    mov [es:si], eax

    inc di                      ; t++
    pop cx
    loop .t_loop

    ; 2. Softmax over attention scores
    ; Converts raw R_ATT[h][0..pos] to probabilities
.softmax:
    xchg cx, di
    call get_att_ptr            ; SI = &R_ATT[h][0]
    xchg di, si

    ; Find max score
    push di
    push cx
.max:
    scasd                       ; DI += 4, compare eax
    cmovl eax, [es:di-4]        ; new max
    loop .max
    pop cx
    pop di

.max_found:
    ; Compute exp(x - max) for each score and accumulate sum
    push di
    push cx
.s_exp:
    push eax                    ; save max
    sub eax, [es:di]            ; diff = max - x
    shr eax, 10                 ; scale down for LUT index, diff / 64
    cmp ax, 511                 ; clamp to LUT range
    jle .s_ok
    mov ax, 511
.s_ok:
    xchg ax, bx
    shl bx, 2                   ; bx = index * 4
    mov eax, [fs:bx]            ; eax = exp_lut[diff]
    add esi, eax                ; sum += exp
    stosd                       ; replace score with exp, DI += 4
    pop eax                     ; restore max
    loop .s_exp

    ; Divide each exp by sum
    pop cx
    pop di
.s_div:
    mov eax, [es:di]
    movzx edx, word [es:di+2]   ; edx:eax = exp value as FP32.16
    shl eax, 16
    div esi                     ; eax = exp / sum (FP16.16)
    stosd                       ; store probability, DI += 4
    loop .s_div
    ; 3. Weighted sum of V
    ; out[h] = sum over t of (attention[h][t] * V[t])
.agg:
    ; Clear r_xb[h] before accumulating
    imul ax, bp, 32             ; h * 32
    mov ah, R_XB >> 8
    xchg ax, di
    xor ax, ax
    mov cl, HEAD_DIM * 2
    rep stosw                   ; zero out R_XB[h]

    call zero_di_jmp_get_pos_count ; DI = t
.v_loop:
    push cx

    ; Load V vector for token t, KV head kvh = h/2
    mov dx, VC_SEG
    call call_set_seg_1024_jmp_get_kv_offset ; DS = V cache, BX = offset of V[t][kvh]

    ; a_t = R_ATT[h][t]
    call get_att_ptr            ; SI = &R_ATT[h][t]
    es lodsd                    ; eax = a_t

    ; Dequantize V: multiply a_t by V scale for token t
    push ds
    push dx
    mov dx, VS_SEG
    call set_seg_128            ; DS = V scale cache for this layer
    pop si                      ; t * 4 from get_att_ptr
    imul dword [si]             ; multiply by scale_vt
    pop ds                      ; restore DS = VC_SEG

    call q16_shift              ; eax = a_scaled = a_t * scale_vt

    ; Accumulate: R_XB[h] += a_scale * V[t]
    xchg edx, eax               ; edx = a_scaled
    imul ax, bp, 32             ; h * 32
    mov ah, R_XB >> 8
    xchg ax, si                 ; SI = &R_XB[h]

    mov cl, HEAD_DIM
.v_mac:
    movsx eax, byte [bx]        ; eax = V[t][i] (int8)
    inc bx
    imul eax, edx               ; eax = V[t][i] * a_scaled
    add [es:si], eax
    lodsd                       ; SI += 4, value is dead
    loop .v_mac

    inc di                      ; t++
    pop cx
    loop .v_loop

    ; Next head
    dec bp
    jns .head_loop
.done:
    ret
